subject: Marketplace governance + integration workbook for GCP & Azure listing
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace questionnaire — kickoff and owners

Hi team,

Acme's procurement just sent us a combined GCP/Azure marketplace questionnaire that mixes procurement (billing models, private offers) with security/compliance asks (data residency, SOC2). They want a consolidated workbook back by EOD Tuesday 4/13.

Key asks I noted:
- Marketplace listing eligibility (partner registration, marketplace terms)
- Billing and metering: SaaS metered billing vs. BYOL, private offers and invoicing cadence
- Integration: marketplace metering hooks, metered products, Offer APIs (Azure Marketplace, GCP Marketplace)
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 attestation, encryption in transit/at rest, VPC options, data residency options per region
- Contracting: master agreement, private offer template, PO / SOW flow

Can you two split this out? Karthik: marketplace integration, metering hooks, and private-offer flow (Azure/GCP specifics). Monica: procurement/contracting and security/compliance evidence (SOC2 summary, data residency). I will own the consolidated workbook and final send.

I attached the initial questionnaire and the Acme procurement email.

Thanks,
Karthik
---
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace questionnaire — kickoff and owners

Thanks Karthik — quick notes from procurement/compliance side:

- SOC 2: we have an auditors' summary (SOC2 Type II, report period Jan 2026–Dec 2026). I can include a one-page summary and the auditor contact for full report disclosure under NDA.
- Data residency: Hosted API supports region pinning in us-west1/us-east4/eu-west1; Dedicated/Private can be deployed to customer VPC on prem or to specific cloud region; we need to call out that we can offer on-prem via our Private package (longer lead time).
- Encryption: TLS1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest; KMS integrations available (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) when using Dedicated/Private.
- Audit logs: Console provides 90 days by default; enterprise retention add-on available for 13 months.

Attachments I'll provide: SOC2_Summary_Redwood.pdf; data-residency-table.csv (will include in the workbook).

Question for procurement: Does Acme require a FedRAMP-equivalent or specific regional compliance? I'll flag any gaps.

—Monica
Manager, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-corp.com>, Cloud Marketplace Onboarding <marketplace-team@cloudhub.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace governance + integration workbook for GCP & Azure listing

Hi Maria / Acme procurement,

Thanks for the questionnaire — attaching our consolidated workbook (RFI_Responses_Redwood_GCP_Azure.xlsx) and a short appendix with the marketplace integration checklist. Highlights:

- Marketplace registration: Redwood is an approved partner on Azure and GCP partner programs; we can submit the publisher registration artifacts within 2 business days.
- Billing models: We support meter-based SaaS billing via the GCP Marketplace Metering API (containerized & SaaS offerings) and Azure Marketplace SaaS Fulfillment with private offers enabled. For committed/reserved capacity customers, we recommend our Dedicated SKU with monthly billing and invoicing via private offer.
- Private offers: We can accept private offers for both Azure and GCP; templates included (azure-marketplace-private-offer-template.docx). For private offers we prefer PO -> DocuSign -> private-offer activation flow; our legal team has a standard private-offer addendum.
- Integration hooks: We outlined required webhook endpoints, token rotation, and expected payloads in the workbook. Karthik will follow up with payload examples and sample code.

Next steps:
1) Monica to attach SOC2 summary and data-residency table (by EOD 4/12).
2) Karthik to populate marketplace metering details and private-offer activation steps (by 4/12).
3) I will route the workbook to Acme procurement and marketplace contacts, and propose a 30-minute technical sync on 4/13 to confirm metering and billing flows.

If that schedule doesn't work, please suggest alternate times.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: RFI_Responses_Redwood_GCP_Azure.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: azure-marketplace-private-offer-template.docx (docx)

From: GCP Partner Ops <gcp-partner@bigcorp.com>

Cc: Marketplace Onboarding <marketplace-team@cloudhub.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace governance + integration workbook for GCP & Azure listing

Sean,

Thanks for the workbook. A couple of clarifications from GCP side:
- Metering & Usage Reporting: please ensure you expose the SaaS usage report endpoint that conforms to the GCP Marketplace Metering API v2 (we listed required fields in the attachment). We flagged the need for idempotency keys for retries.
- Identity: OAuth2 service account flow is preferred for automated metering writes; if you plan to use customer-bound credentials, document the fallback.
- Private Offer Flow: GCP requires a populated Offer ID at activation; we can accept the private-offer template but need the pricing SKU mapping.

We can do the 30-minute sync at 10:00am PT tomorrow (4/13) to walk through the payload examples.

Cheers,
GCP Partner Ops

Great sync today — thanks everyone for the fast turnaround. Follow-up notes:

- Action items completed/assigned:
  * Karthik: uploaded payload examples and sample webhook code to the shared Drive, included idempotency & retry guidance.
  * Monica: uploaded SOC2_Summary_Redwood.pdf and the data residency matrix.
  * Sean/AE: submitted the consolidated workbook to Acme procurement and linked the DocuSign private-offer packet (link below).

- Outstanding items for Acme procurement: please confirm preferred billing model (metered SaaS vs. monthly prepay for Dedicated) and whether invoicing through marketplace or direct invoicing is required. This will determine whether we configure metering mapping or prepare a private-offer invoice template.

Links and attachments: DocuSign private-offer packet: https://docusign.com/packet/abc123
Shared Drive (RFI workbook + payload examples): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1_example_rfi_folder

If Acme is ready, we can accept a PO and start the private-offer activation within 3 business days (for standard private offers) — Dedicated/private deployments have longer lead times (2–4 weeks depending on region and network provisioning).

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
